summary: The charter of the ARPANET Users Interest Working Group, called USING, formed at a May 1973 meeting of 15 network people to improve the network user's working environment. It sets out the group's background and aim of representing user needs.

eli5.summary: A group of people who use the network formed a club to speak up for users. This is the paper saying who they are and what they want.

subtitle: A working group formed to represent network users' interests

tldr.problem: ARPANET was growing beyond research and development into a service, but the people building the network needed to better understand and respond to what users actually wanted.
tldr.mechanism: A group called USING (ARPANET Users Interest Working Group) was formed to represent user needs, collect feedback, and push for improvements to user-facing services like documentation, command languages and consulting help.
tldr.outcome: The group set goals to make ARPANET a coherent system where users could regulate their own working environment, with plans for standards like a Common Command Language and a handbook for new users.

today: RFC 584 was the charter of the ARPANET Users Interest Working Group, which no longer operates. The RFC is an early document showing how ARPANET's builders were beginning to think about user experience as a key part of the network's success.

sections.title: Forming a User Advocacy Group
sections.content:
The ARPANET Users Interest Working Group (USING) was formed at a meeting on May 23, 1973, with 15 network people aiming to improve the network user's working environment. The group recognised that ARPANET was becoming a service, not just a research platform, and that its viability depended on user satisfaction. USING would represent the interests and needs of the Network community, making sure builders heard what users actually wanted.

Alongside USING, a broader group called USERS was created as a forum for any interested person to air complaints, exchange information and make proposals. USING served as a steering committee and lobby for USERS, forwarding ideas to the right people.
sections.eli5: Network builders realised they needed to listen to the people who actually used the network, so they started a group called USING to speak up for users.

sections.title: Scope and Membership
sections.content:
USING membership is open to individuals able and willing to make meaningful contributions to improving network user support. USING's scope covers all facets of Network activity that affect services to users: the availability of resources, their reliability and ease of use.

This includes everything from how friendly the system documentation is, to what commands users can type, to whether people are available to help when things go wrong.
sections.eli5: USING focuses on all the things that make the network easy or hard to use: good guides, simple commands, and people ready to help.

sections.title: Short-Term Objectives and Vision
sections.content:
USING's overall goal is to ensure ARPANET becomes a coherent system in which users can regulate their own working environment according to their experience level and desired transparency. System resources should be self-documenting, and assistance at all levels should be available and user-controlled.

For the first 6 to 12 months, the group set specific targets: specifying a user-level Common Command Language (so users didn't have to learn a different language at each site), designing a network editor, further defining user issues, encouraging user consulting services, and publishing a handbook for new users.
sections.eli5: USING wanted the network to be easy for beginners but not annoying for experts, with all the help and tools built in.

sections.title: Long-Term Vision
sections.content: Beyond the immediate objectives, USING planned long-term activities including monitoring and spurring user-oriented development efforts like resource directories, tutorials, training courses and referral services. The group would create mechanisms to encourage and respond to user feedback, develop profiles of user requirements and usage patterns, and work to lower the barrier to entry for new users.
sections.eli5: In the years ahead, they wanted to keep listening to users and keep making the network more friendly and educational for everyone.
